pairs.difference: B: each gauge and button sits inside doubled, concentric dark rings, a heavy tracked bevel runs round the faceplate, and the tread-plate floor is a stamped field of crisp marks of equal strength. A: the awning and brass posts have thinner lines that vary in weight, with lost edges on the white stripes and posts, and the strongest edges stay on the scalloped awning and wheel.
pairs.fix: Remove the double rims around the gauges and buttons: each button meets the panel with one thin soft shadow line. Let the lit top edge of the panel fade into the background. Make the floor tread pattern faint and blurred, far weaker than the panel.

pairs.difference: B: the visor rim and collar are parallel, evenly sharp tracked lines, with a closed contour round the shell and no lost edge on the lit side. A: the shoes have busier internal lines, but the weight varies between laces, mesh and sole. Both show a hard horizon line and an outline reading just below the real range, so that measure does not separate them.
pairs.fix: Draw the visor rim as one thin seam, not two parallel lines. Let the top of the white helmet soften and partly melt into the background, and keep the sharpest edge only where the visor meets the shell.

pairs.difference: The signals conflict. A has a uniform dark inset line round the player face and heavy contours along the earphone cable, which resemble the generated lessons. B has soft, broken contours and lost edges on the dome and hull, which resemble the real cards, but its background density of 0.003 sits just under the real floor because the rings are very faint. Neither card clearly reads as generated on edges.

Both cards have the same treatment: thick dark rings around the portholes, a strong seam (A's hull rim, B's riveted bands), and thinner contours on the softer parts (A's tail fin, B's red fins). Densities are almost equal at 0.12 and 0.126. Nothing on the edges separates them.

B: every thatch shingle is ringed with a dark line, and the pool ripples, tile rim and stool rings are drawn as strongly as the drinks, so there is no edge hierarchy. Background density of 0.144 is well above the real 0.089 maximum, though the frame-filling scene may inflate it. A: the dome has quieter thin lines, and the strongest edges gather on the door and tube, although the crater rims are fairly dark.
pairs.fix: Paint the thatch as grouped soft masses with only a few crisp shingle tips near the front. Blur the pool ripples and tiles into soft colour shapes, so the sharpest edges stay on the fruit and glasses.

pairs.difference: A: a closed, even, dark contour runs round the whole ring and planet, the colour bands are drawn as clean curved lines, and the crater rim is a crisp dark ellipse, like an inked sticker. B: the contours are broken, with the far sole edges fading out, and only the strap undersides and sole holes carry dark accents, like the lost-and-found edges on real cards.
pairs.fix: Remove the even dark contour around the ring and planet. Let the lit upper edge of the ring soften into the background, and make the boundaries between the orange bands soft colour transitions with no line.

pairs.difference: A is the rose arch shown among the real cards in image 1, and its density of 0.317 comes from many petals and leaves, so the high reading does not mark it as generated. B: the crack and plaque frame are dark and heavy, but the fluted shaft has soft edges and a partly lost right side, and all its measures are within range. No edge reason marks B as generated.

B: the meteor's contour is thin and nervous with a fine grainy texture across the rock, the flames barely hold an edge, and subject density of 0.027 and outline of -0.09 are both below the real range. A: the scarf has firm tail contours but soft, clean interior folds and a crisp badge as the focus, and its numbers are in range.
pairs.fix: Give the rock a confident, smooth silhouette with soft edges on the lit side. Remove the fine speckle from its surface, make the crater rims clean, and give the nearest flame tips a crisp edge.

pairs.difference: A: an even, closed dark line follows the entire dish rim and base, and the clouds and rocks are also outlined, while subject density of 0.066 sits below the real floor of 0.076. B: the castle has more internal detail in range, with softer silhouette edges and the edges melting into the sand at the bucket and walls.
pairs.fix: Break the dark line round the dish: keep a crisp edge only at the feed and struts, and let the lit rim fade softly into the sky. Draw the clouds and small rocks as soft shapes with no contour.

pairs.difference: A: the water and pavers have sharp broken lines, and background density of 0.046 is at the real ceiling, but that is still in range. B: the car's stripe and body seams are heavy, with softer left and floor edges. Each has the kind of edge hierarchy seen on real cards, and all measures are in range.

B: a continuous inked dark line runs along the tube and down all three tripod legs at nearly the same weight, and the ground is peppered with fine speckle marks. A: the plank gaps are strong, but the binocular body has lost edges on the lit far barrel and its weight changes from the heavy lens rims to the faint body contour.
pairs.fix: Drop the dark line along the telescope tube and tripod legs: let the lit side fade softly and leave only the shadow side defined. Keep the crisp edge for the brass rims, and render the ground as soft mottled tones without speckle.

pairs.difference: A: the windshield and door windows have thick doubled frames, the grille is densely lined and the road dashes are outlined in black. Subject density of 0.203 is above the real 0.179 ceiling and outline of 0.084 is near the top of the range. B: the rover body and tyres are softer and in range, though its contour is fairly closed and the ground is speckled.
pairs.fix: Thin the window frames to one fine seam, simplify the grille into a few soft bars, and paint the road dashes as plain soft-edged shapes with no dark border.

pattern: The generated tell is uniformity, not any single hard line. Lesson fakes keep a closed, even contour around the hero with no lost edge on the lit side. Their seams and rims are doubled as parallel tracked lines around buttons, visors, windows and portholes, and their secondary surfaces (wood grain, waves, ground speckle, tread) are nearly as crisp as the focus. Real cards vary line weight, let lit edges fade into the background and keep the background quiet. The density numbers overlap heavily and a real card can exceed the range (the rose arch in p07), so closed contours and doubled seams are stronger evidence than the numbers. Several pairs here are weak or conflicting on edges alone.
